**Timing**: 96 BPM, 4/4. Every note-event (whether a single note in a scale run, or the mega-chord) lasts exactly 2 bars = 5.0 seconds.

**Per instrument folder structure**:
```
{instrument}/
  chromatic/
    {instrument}_chromatic_scale.mid   (every semitone in range, sequential)
    {instrument}_chromatic_chord.mid   (every semitone in range, one giant stacked cluster)
  major/

  minor/
    A/  ...  (all 12 keys)
  diminished/
    C/  ...  (all 12 keys)
  augmented/
    C/  ...  (all 12 keys)
```

The `_chord` files stack **every note of that key's scale across the instrument's entire range** simultaneously — so e.g. a piano `C_major_chord.mid` fires all 52 C-major-scale notes from A0 to C8 at once as one massive cluster chord, held for 5 seconds. The `_scale` files are the sequential version (same notes, one at a time, 5 sec each).

chat:
12 PDFs, one per instrument, engraved with LilyPond (proper notation software, not a MIDI-to-notation converter — hence genuinely clean output). Clef handling by instrument:

| Instrument | Clef treatment |
|---|---|
| Electric Guitar | Treble clef with ottava (8), sounds an octave lower than written |
| Bass Guitar | Bass clef with ottava (8), sounds an octave lower than written |
| Piano/Keys | True grand staff, split at middle C |
| Vocals | Treble clef |
| Violin | Treble clef |
| Viola | Alto clef, switches to treble above A4 |
| Cello | Bass → tenor → treble as the range ascends |
| Double Bass | Bass clef with ottava (8), sounds an octave lower than written |
| Trumpet Bb | Treble clef, **transposed** (written a major 2nd above concert pitch) |
| French Horn | Treble clef, **transposed** (written a perfect 5th above concert pitch) |
| Trombone | Bass clef, switches to tenor above middle C |
| Tuba | Bass clef, no transposition |

Each PDF has a footer noting the transposition/octave convention where relevant, so nothing's ambiguous to a reader picking it up cold.

One thing worth flagging: I used straight quarter notes at a plain 4/4 pulse for the notation — the actual 5-second-per-note timing from the MIDI files doesn't translate to normal notation (nobody writes a scale in whole notes tied across multiple bars), so I treated this as a standalone reference chart rather than a literal transcription of the audio timing. Let me know if you'd rather it show a tempo marking or some other reference back to the MIDI files.
